AI NEWS DAILY — 4 November 2026

TOP STORY
Google's Gemini 4 Carbon takes #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59, one point ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and two ahead of GPT-6 Astra — at a lower cost per task. Independent SemiAnalysis GDPx testing is less flattering: Carbon trails Opus 5.5 on agentic work. Access is limited to vetted cyber defenders via the Fairwind program for now.

5 KEY UPDATES
1. Meituan ships LongCat-2.5: 1.6T parameters, native multimodal, trained entirely on Chinese accelerators. API-only at $0.30/$1.20 per M tokens.
2. MiniMax M3 launches as the first open-weight model with frontier coding, 1M context and native multimodality together. Weights promised on Hugging Face.
3. Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.8T total, 104B active) opens its weights today; Mistral Large 4 and a DeepSeek V4 preview also went open this week.
4. Anthropic's amended S-1/A: ~$17B Q3 revenue, ~$26B full-year forecast, and $895B of compute commitments through 2031 — with risk factors warning it may imminently cross its own recursive self-improvement threshold.
5. MIT CSAIL had GPT-6 Astra rewrite another model's weights directly, lifting Qwen3.5-0.8B from 7.9% to 48.1% on MATH-500 by changing 0.016% of parameters.

CONCEPT OF THE DAY
Sparse attention: how 1M-token context became cheap. Dense attention quadruples in cost when you double context; sparse methods let each token attend to a chosen subset instead. DeepSeek uses DSA plus token compression, MiniMax uses MSA, Zyphra uses a tree index — all three made a million tokens affordable, but capacity is not the same thing as comprehension.
